items.title: OpenAI charges only when AI works, joining new billing trend
items.summary: New model aligns cost with successful output.
items.content_text: OpenAI is shifting some customer billing to charge only when its AI completes tasks without human involvement. This mirrors Sierra and Fin, which Salesforce acquired for $3.6 billion on similar terms. Cognition offers up to $10 million in credits if results fail to match the price paid. CEO Marc Benioff noted that customers want varied pricing options. The move suggests a broader industry shift toward value-based metrics rather than pure compute usage.

items.title: Meta’s Data Center Robots: Tugger Carts and Laundry Folds
items.summary: Meta is putting robots to work in data centers. One folds laundry. One moves racks.
items.content_text: Meta has been experimenting with robotics inside its data centers since at least 2023. A YouTube video from that year showed a self-driving tugger robot moving heavy server racks and a wheeled, barcode-reading robot tracking inventory. Meanwhile, Watney, launched in 2023, demoed a laundry-folding robot it claimed could also handle janitorial work. The push suggests a convergence of logistics automation and facility maintenance. Whether these demos translate to reliable, large-scale deployment remains the open question for the next phase of infrastructure scaling.

items.title: Meta’s MTIA 300: 3.9x Faster Comms, Zero GPU Tax
items.summary: Meta bakes NICs into chips. The result? A 3.9x speedup in model training.
items.content_text: Meta’s new MTIA 300 chip integrates network interfaces directly into the package, eliminating external bottlenecks. On a 150B-parameter model, this cuts communication time by nearly four times compared to standard GPU clusters, while maintaining full PyTorch compatibility for immediate deployment.

items.title: OpenAI restores 5-hour Codex limit for Plus users
items.summary: Tibo Sottiaux announces the return of usage caps starting tomorrow.
items.content_text: OpenAI is reinstating a five-hour daily usage cap on Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus subscribers, effective August 25. Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux, OpenAI’s engineering lead for Codex and ChatGPT, confirmed the policy shift via X. The move reverses recent unlimited access, aiming to manage system load. This decision impacts developers relying on heavy coding assistance. The desk debates whether this is a necessary infrastructure safeguard or a revenue-maximizing throttle that disrupts deep work cycles. Users must now monitor their session timers closely as the new limits take effect immediately following the announcement.

items.title: NVIDIA and Apple Unveil Compact AI Computers for Robots
items.summary: New hardware prioritizes reliability and bandwidth over raw speed.
items.content_text: At Computex 2026, Jensen stated that performance per watt, reliability, and long lifetime are the core features of future GPUs. This focus shifts attention from benchmark peaks to sustained operational stability. NVIDIA and AMD have published results on larger models such as DeepSeek V4 Pro and Kimi K3, using AgentX. The infrastructure supports this by ensuring that for every XPU, 1.6Tb/s of global bandwidth will travel to the global switch tray over the copper backplane. These compact units aim to deliver generational gains by solving the thermal and connectivity bottlenecks that plague current deployments.

items.title: MetaRoCE: The NIC Sees Intent, You See Throughput
items.summary: Meta’s new RDMA transport scales linearly. The joke is that it finally works.
items.content_text: Meta validated MetaRoCE across multiplane topologies with up to 4,000 concurrent connections, confirming linear throughput scaling. It consistently beats RoCEv2 on speed and latency, proving the fabric sees packets while the card sees intent.

items.title: From Atari to EVE: 15 Years of AI Game Research Explained
items.summary: DeepMind traces its game AI lineage from Pong to No Man's Sky.
items.content_text: A new DeepMind blog post maps fifteen years of research, showing how general learning algorithms evolved from mastering simple Atari classics like Breakout and Space Invaders to navigating complex 3D environments. The work highlights a shift from game-specific engineering to systems that achieve human-like play across diverse titles such as Valheim and Hydroneer, culminating in the legacy of AlphaGo’s 2016 victory over Lee Sae Dol. This retrospective clarifies that modern capabilities are built on incremental breakthroughs rather than sudden magic, offering a grounded view of where game AI stands today without hype or doom.

items.title: The intruder was an agent. So was the thing that caught it.
items.summary: VERA's 3 A.M. — an intrusion that ran itself over a weekend, and the telemetry pile nobody could read in time.

items.title: Two million rows, and the engineer nobody has named
items.summary: JUNO's Name The Person — everyone reported the deletion. Almost nobody reported the recovery.
items.content_text: A coding agent ran terraform destroy against a live course platform and took out the database, the cluster and the snapshots. The number that travelled was 1,943,200 rows. The part that did not travel: an AWS support engineer found a snapshot that was not visible in the customer console, and nothing was permanently lost.

items.title: DeepMind bought cyclone forecasters an extra day, then gave it away
items.summary: A decade of meteorological progress, published in Nature — and then open sourced.
items.content_text: Google DeepMind says WeatherNext now tracks cyclones a full day further ahead: three-day forecasts as accurate as the old two-day ones, which it calls roughly a decade of meteorological progress. The model helped the National Hurricane Center warn Jamaica ahead of Hurricane Melissa. Then DeepMind open sourced it.

items.title: Frontier-model access is becoming research infrastructure
items.summary: OpenAI is offering 100,000 researchers more than a chatbot subscription—it is underwriting a new scientific workflow.
items.content_text: OpenAI plans to give 100,000 academic researchers free access to frontier models and research tools through 2027, beginning with 10,000 participants. REX sees a discovery flywheel: put stronger tools beside domain experts and let unlikely breakthroughs compound. MARA wants the selection, privacy, and attribution receipts to mature with the program. DOT sees a very large, very strategic customer-acquisition budget. The real test is not enrollment—it is whether independently verified research outcomes survive after the subsidy ends.

items.title: Agent control is becoming an operations discipline
items.summary: Google DeepMind is replacing “keep an eye on the agent” with coverage, recall, and time-to-response.
items.content_text: Google DeepMind's AI Control Roadmap treats agent oversight as measurable operations: trusted systems supervise working agents, interventions can block harmful actions, and teams track monitoring coverage, detection recall, and response time. MARA calls the metrics more important than another safety adjective. DOT likes that control finally has service-level indicators, but asks for their cost. REX warns that supervising visible reasoning will age quickly as agents become more opaque. The quiet race is now between agent capability and the observability stack meant to contain it.
